reason: The support cells and collagen fibers appear to be the pieces for building the skin's supporting tissue.
expectation: They will form a supportive skin layer.

effect: The fibers and support cells formed a skin layer with capillaries, leaving the surface barrier to build.
reaction: The tug panels make the fibers’ supporting role clearer.
reason: Cell junctions appear suited to joining the loose surface cells into a layer.
expectation: The junctions will connect the surface cells into a more continuous layer.

effect: The surface cells now form a connected sheet, but water still escapes, so it needs a barrier.
reaction: The escaping water makes the remaining problem clear.
reason: The tough outer layer has lipids between its cells and looks suited to limiting water loss from the connected surface.
expectation: The outer layer will help reduce water loss through the surface.

effect: The outer layer reduced water loss, so the barrier can now be joined to the supporting skin tissue.
reaction: The comparison of water arrows makes the barrier's effect clear.
reason: The surface barrier and supporting skin layer appear to be complementary layers of the skin.
expectation: They will form a layered skin structure.

effect: The barrier and supporting layer now form layered skin, with vessels beneath the living surface cells. The skin still needs sensory endings.
reaction: The inset makes the separation between vessels and surface cells clear.
reason: The sensory endings appear suited to giving the layered skin a sense of contact.
expectation: The endings will add touch sensing to the skin.

effect: The skin now detects contact, but its sensory nerve still needs a connection to the nervous system, and the arm needs continuing supplies.
reaction: The dashed gap makes the missing connection clear.
reason: The arm already has a nervous system connection, so it seems the natural place to connect the sensitive skin.
expectation: The skin will join the arm and connect its touch information to the nervous system.

effect: Touch information now reaches the spinal cord, and the arm's vessel ends still need the body supply network.
reaction: The separate insets make the connected nerve and remaining supply gap clear.
reason: The body supply network can connect to the arm's waiting vessel ends.
expectation: The circulation will supply the skin-covered arm with oxygen and nutrients.

effect: The arm now receives continuing supplies, and the remaining goal is to use contact feedback to hold the glass.
reaction: The separate nerve and blood pathways make their different roles clear.
reason: The living body model has the connected touch and motor systems needed to interact with the glass.
expectation: The model will use contact feedback to hold the glass steady.

effect: The model used touch feedback and muscle tension to steady the slipping glass, completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: The slipping-glass sequence made the purpose of touch feedback concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was most worthwhile because the slipping and correction connected touch, nerves and muscle work to a familiar action.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the surface barrier to the supporting layer felt straightforward, though the resulting cross-section clarified where the vessels lie.

surprise.text: The connected surface cells still allowed water to escape; adding the outer layer reduced, but did not eliminate, water loss.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary. The item names and picture descriptions generally indicated how the pieces fit.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it used another familiar action to show how body systems work together. The glass sequence gave those connections a clear purpose.
